# Goban Studio v15.0.0

v15 is about how the app feels in the hand: a board that looks and
behaves like wood and stone, a word on every move you play, pages that
use a large window, and an engine that is stronger and, where the
computer allows, faster. It also fixes what the v14 review found. v15
reads everything v9–v14 saved; nothing has to be converted.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. **v15 needs macOS 13 or
later** (it said 11, but the toolchain and the faster engine need 13).
Windows on ARM runs the x64 build under the system's emulation. Your
games, progress and settings are kept outside the app — in
`~/Library/Application Support/dev.hxddh.gobanstudio` on macOS and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.hxddh.gobanstudio\Data` on Windows — so replacing the
app keeps them.

## The board

- **Wood.** The board has a quiet straight grain instead of a flat
  colour, an edge that catches the light, and a shadow close to the table.
- **Lines and star points** are sized from the board: a 19×19 board on a
  Retina screen no longer has half-pixel lines, and its star points can
  be seen.
- **A stone lands.** A new stone comes down and its shadow closes in under
  it, instead of popping in. At 19×19 sizes the white stones' shell lines
  no longer turn to noise.
- **The pointer** shows a light stone with a clear edge where you would
  play, and the last move's ring no longer outweighs the stone.
- **The dark board** keeps the warmth of the wood, with the light falling
  off towards the edges; white stones are barely dimmed and black stones
  need no rim.
- **Settings → Board** can put the coordinates on all four sides, and can
  give the board traditional proportions: rows a little further apart than
  columns, as on a real board, so its squares look square from your seat.
- **The stone sound** is brighter: a harder, shorter contact, closer to a
  stone on kaya.

## Playing

- **A word on every move.** When the game teaches, or the balance is
  shown, the panel says how your last move compared with the best one —
  good, slack or a mistake, with the points — and the move list marks
  slack moves and mistakes. It costs no extra search. The balance is shown
  by default for new players, and the result of a game says how your
  moves went.
- **No weak moves from a busy engine.** With the human-style network
  installed, the computer could sometimes play a much weaker move, and a
  review could come back empty, because two requests to KataGo cut each
  other off. They now wait their turn, and a request that is cut off is
  asked again instead of counting as a failure.
- **The stronger network is newer.** "Stronger analysis" downloads
  KataGo's `kata1-b18c384nbt` network (98 MB) instead of the 2020 one, from
  katagotraining.org; reviews, hints and the count are better for it.
- **Faster where it can be.** On Windows the engine uses the AVX2 build on
  processors that have it; on Apple Silicon it uses KataGo's Metal build.
  Either falls back to the plain build by itself if it cannot start.
- The offline engine stops at the end of a game instead of playing into
  your territory.

## Pages

- **Large windows** show Today and the Library in two columns.
- **The Library** lists the game on the board before it is saved, and each
  classic shows its final position.
- **Today** shows this week as seven days, today's practice as a goal, and
  — before there is anything else to show — a problem to try.
- **Practice** shows each unit with its first position and each unit's and
  topic's progress as a bar. In a topic, the stones a problem is about
  carry a triangle, and every tile is framed the same, so stones are the
  same size.
- A row's own action (Start, Continue) looks like a button. A verdict, a
  hint and the day's goal ease in instead of popping.
- Places cross-fade where the system supports it (not with reduced motion).
- Reading text in lessons and explanations is a size larger, and the
  language choice in Settings looks like every other choice.
- On macOS the window's title bar follows the app's light or dark setting.

## Fixed

- **A game with undo stays unrated.** Redoing the move no longer made it
  count again after the app had said it would not.
- **Practice** keeps a place for a new problem while the reviews due are
  no more than twice the day's size.
- **SGF.** A `CA[…]` inside a comment is no longer read as the file's
  encoding; `PL` is written even without set-up stones; two passes in the
  middle of a record no longer end its review.
- **Undo after deleting a game** no longer silently does nothing after a
  backup: the app says the game is now deleted for good.
- **KataGo that was not ready at start** is looked for again, instead of
  leaving the offline engine for the whole session.
- A click on the board in the moment after the computer's reply could be
  ignored. It is not.
- The licences of the networks are stated correctly: the built-in network
  is CC0, the downloaded ones are under the KataGo Neural Network License,
  which ships with the app.

## Under the hood

- The desktop shell is split into modules by concern, and built with
  Native SDK 0.11.1. The interface runs on Preact 11.
- Model downloads may follow redirects only to the hosts named for them,
  over HTTPS; updates still only to GitHub.
- Tests no longer depend on the day they run.
- **A save survives a power cut**, not just a crash: each file is flushed
  to the disk (on macOS with a full flush) and so is its folder after the
  rename.
- The interface is type-checked, every hook's dependencies are checked,
  and a move or a problem attempt re-renders a third as much as before.
- The shell's installer and engine code are split by concern.

## Known limits

- **Not checked by people.** The new board, the move verdicts and the
  wide pages have not been through a usability test or a strong player's
  review, and the new strings in Chinese, Korean and Japanese are the
  developer's own.
- **Platform code has not been tried by hand.** The Metal and AVX2
  engines and their fallback, and the macOS title bar following the app's
  appearance, compile and pass their tests, but nobody has run them on a
  real Mac or PC. The strongest level and the stronger network's visit
  budget are to be measured again with the new network.
- **The builds are not code-signed.** macOS and Windows warn on first
  launch; the README in each download says what to do. There is still no
  update signing key.
- **There is no Windows installer.** The download is a zip.
- **The opening book** was made with the 2020 network and still lacks the
  Chinese opening.
- **No Traditional Chinese interface.**
- **Content.** 15 of the 20 classics have only their headline note; the
  problem bank tops out at about 5 kyu.
